artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let G be a finite non-abelian simple group and set D = G. For each pair (a,b) ∈ D × D let |ab| denote the order of the element ab ∈ G. For a positive integer t, define
   Aut_t(Γ) = { τ ∈ Sym(D) : for all a,b ∈ D, |ab| = t  ⇔  |a^τ · b^τ| = t },
i.e. the set of permutations of D that preserve the relation "the product has order t". Define
   Aut(Γ) = ⋂_{t ≥ 1} Aut_t(Γ),
the group of permutations of D preserving the order of every product. Let p be the second smallest prime divisor of |G| (so 2 and p are the two minimal prime divisors of |G|).

Question: Is it true that for every finite non-abelian simple group G one has
   Aut(Γ) = Aut_2(Γ) ∩ Aut_p(Γ)?
That is, is a permutation of G that preserves the set of pairs whose product has order 2 and the set of pairs whose product has order p automatically order-preserving on all products?
